facts.claim: Anthropic: everything in the request counts toward the context window: the system prompt, every message (tool results and documents included), the tool definitions, and the reply the model writes.
Anthropic's current Claude models have a context window of up to 1M tokens, depending on the model; older ones have 200k.
Anthropic: if the input alone exceeds the model's context window, the API refuses the request as too long.
Anthropic: more context isn't automatically better; as the token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade, which it calls context rot.
Chroma tested 18 models (July 2025) and found performance varies significantly as input length changes, even on simple tasks.
Chroma: one related but wrong passage lowers accuracy against the fact alone, four lower it further, and distractors do not all hurt equally.
Liu and colleagues (2023) found models do best when the needed information is at the beginning or end of the input, and degrade significantly when it sits in the middle of a long context.
Anthropic's context-engineering guide: find the smallest possible set of high-signal tokens that maximize the likelihood of the outcome you want.
Anthropic's context-engineering guide: agents can keep lightweight references (file paths, stored queries) and load the data just in time, when they need it.
Anthropic: prompt caching covers the whole prompt in the order tools, system, messages, up to and including the block marked as a cache breakpoint.
Anthropic: a change at one level invalidates that level and every level after it; changing a tool definition invalidates the whole cache.
Anthropic: a request can set up to 4 cache breakpoints.
Anthropic: writing to the 5-minute cache costs 1.25 times the base input token price.
Anthropic: writing to the 1-hour cache costs 2 times the base input token price.
Anthropic: reading from the cache costs 0.1 times the base input token price (some newer models less: 0.05 or 0.025 times).
Anthropic: the cache lives 5 minutes by default (1 hour on request), and each use refreshes it at no extra cost.
Anthropic: a prompt shorter than the model's minimum (512 to 4,096 tokens, by model) is not cached, even when marked.
Anthropic's price list charges 5 times the base input price for each output token on every current Claude model.
OpenAI caches prompts automatically, from 1,024 tokens on its newest models, and charges reused tokens at a discount of 90% on most of those models, up to 95% on one.
OpenAI: put stable instructions and shared reference material first and dynamic content, like timestamps, at the end, because a cache hit needs the whole prefix to match.

Anthropic's context editing can clear old tool results once the context passes a threshold (100,000 input tokens by default), keeping the most recent ones (3 by default) and leaving a placeholder where each was.
Anthropic: clearing tool results invalidates the cached prefix, so clear enough at once to be worth a new cache write.
Anthropic's memory tool lets Claude create, read, update and delete files under /memories that persist between conversations.
Anthropic: the memory tool runs client side; Claude asks for file operations and your application carries them out on storage you control.
